label: stellate-pubescent
definition: A pubescent hair quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being covered with short hairs that branch in a star-like manner from a common base.
reason: A very common flora indumentum term (here with the hyphen lost in transcription); PATO has star shaped (PATO:0002065) for the hair but no quality of the hairy surface. Made the same way as glandular-pubescent (FLOPO:0991173).

'Lip bicallose' means the lip has two calli: a count with the counted part in the word. Callus has no part class (the previous review rejected it as generic), so the count cannot be grounded until it has one.

label: homobrochate
definition: A reticulate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the meshes (lumina) of the bearer's reticulum being all of about the same size.
reason: A standard palynological term for the pollen wall (sexine) with a uniform reticulum; no PATO or FLOPO term. Its opposite is heterobrochate.
A compound of two values that both exist: reticulate (FLOPO:0991100) and foveate (PATO:0002296); read as a continuum or combination of the two.
'Pistils not emergent' means not projecting from the flower, i.e. included. It must not be read as the negation of FLOPO:0991193 emergent, which means rising above water.
Bractiferous = bearing bracts, the same as the rule for bracteate.
The glume equals the florets in length: an equality with a second part (florets, flower PO_0009046), not a quality of its own.
A rate of a growth process given without a reference rate. It describes behaviour, not the morphology of the root or branch.
A hyphenated spelling of the existing value. Any number before it ('3-7-palmately-lobed') goes to the count pattern.

'Contracted to apex / to a short stipe' is a narrowing into a named part. PATO:0001500 tapered is defined as gradual and PATO:0001847 constricted is a narrowing in the middle, so neither fits the abrupt reading.
PATO:0002386 anvil has 'anvil shaped' as an EXACT synonym.
Ball-like = globular: PATO:0001499 spherical (synonym globular). The branch example ('curling inward when dry') also needs the specimen-condition pattern.
Balsamic buds and branchlets are coated with a fragrant resin (balsam): FLOPO resinous. The scent alone would be PATO:0002191 aromatic.
A vague likeness with no defined shape or texture; the second example is a fragment about trunk tissue.
Attached by the base = basifixed, for both the ovule and the leaf blade (set against peltate).
Same as the rule for 'expanded' (expanded filament base = dilated), with the base of the part as the bearer (state-of-the-bearer pattern).
Inflated at the base, with the base as the bearer. For a style that is solid-swollen rather than bladdery, PATO:0001571 dilated may fit better.
A bottlebrush inflorescence or branch is brush-like: PATO:0002315, as the rule for penicillate.
A comparison of width with height of the same bearer (crown, whole plant): a ratio of two dimensions, greater than 1.
States where the widest part lies, without fixing the outline. Mapping it to PATO:0001936 obovate would claim an egg-shaped outline the text does not give.
Position of the widest part (at the middle). Not necessarily PATO:0000947 elliptic.
Same as 'broadest near center'.
A compound of two existing values, oblong (PATO:0000946) and obovoid (FLOPO:0991025). 'Broadly' is a degree modifier.
A transcription fragment (words run together); the examples do not contain a quality of that name.
Two values joined: the corolla is streaked (FLOPO:0991206), and the colour (brown) belongs to the lines, not to the corolla.
Bearing bulbils (on caudices, upper stem): the FLOPO bulbil class is present. Where they sit uses the part-of-the-bearer slot.
A loose likeness with different meanings: for a samara, two spreading wings; for a flower, papilionaceous. There is no single shape quality.
A compound of two existing values, campanulate (PATO:0104350) and cup-shaped (PATO:0002227), as in the French 'campanulé-cupuliforme'.
FLOPO:0991010 mat-forming has 'carpet-forming' as a synonym.
A compound of two existing values: ciliated (PATO:0001408) and lanate (PATO:0104357), i.e. margins fringed with woolly hairs.
